units.function: stack two proportional gains, then declare the subject worth modelling

features.clause_structure: two the-more clauses then a thus
original_instantiations: The more developed a record-keeping setup is, the more a firm can draw from its files, and the more of an edge it holds. So the degree to which the records are actually used deserves attention.
A better-run system returns more value and a wider advantage. That is why the level it has reached is worth measuring.

units.source_excerpt: The more mature a D&A system is, the more benefit a corporation can obtain from its database, and the more commercial advantages a company can gain. Thus, the maturity of a D&A system is worthy of attention.
units.reusable_pattern: The more [attribute] a [system] is, the more [gain] and the more [advantage]. Thus, [the attribute] is worthy of attention.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, first paragraph.
stable function: escalate two benefits into a reason to model.
pattern: The more, the more, and the more. Thus, worthy of attention.
boundary: both gains must be real consequences.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reuse the industry or the system name.

units.function: turn the preceding reason into the decision to build the model

original_instantiations: Aware of this, we build a pair of models, one to judge the level and one to raise it, for the client and for firms in other trades.
With that in mind, we set up an assessment and a way to improve it, meant for this company and for others.

units.source_excerpt: Aware of this, we establish a set of assessment and optimization models to assist not only the client, but also corporations in various industries.
units.reusable_pattern: Aware of this, we establish [the models] to assist not only [the client], but also [the wider set].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, first paragraph.
stable function: convert a motive into a build decision and widen the audience.
pattern: Aware of this, we establish / not only / but also.
boundary: the wider set must actually be served later.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name the client.

units.function: open the method list with the first model and its parts

original_instantiations: To begin with, we build the scoring model. We look into the three parts of the system and settle on a dozen indicators, each one given a number.
First we set up the assessment. Three parts are examined and twelve measures are defined, all of them quantified.

units.source_excerpt: To begin with, we establish the assessment model. We investigate into three components and come up with 12 key performance indicators that are strictly quantified.
units.reusable_pattern: To begin with, we establish [the model]. We investigate into [the parts] and come up with [a count] indicators that are strictly quantified.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, second paragraph.
stable function: start the method with a count.
pattern: To begin with, we establish / come up with N that are strictly quantified.
boundary: the count must be exact.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not copy the indicator count.

units.function: name two methods in parallel and say what each does

original_instantiations: The first is a judgement model built on expert grades. The second combines an objective weighting with a subjective one.
One method leans on expert opinion. The other merges two ways of assigning weight.

units.source_excerpt: The first one is the Fuzzy Synthetic Evaluation Model. The second one is the EWM-AHP Method, which is an integrated process of weight calculation.
units.reusable_pattern: The first one is [method A]. The second one is [method B], which is [what it combines].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary.
stable function: present two methods as a pair.
pattern: The first one is / The second one is / which is an integrated process.
boundary: both methods must be used, not merely named.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not copy the method names.

units.function: merge the two scores and turn the result into a level

original_instantiations: Further, we fold the two scores into one and then place the system on a level of the maturity scale.
We combine the two results and, from the combined figure, say which stage the system sits in.

units.source_excerpt: Further, we integrate two scores to obtain the final score, and decide in which level this system locates according to the maturity model.
units.reusable_pattern: Further, we integrate [the two results] to obtain the final [score], and decide in which [level] it locates according to [the scale].
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary.
stable function: convert two numbers into one placement.
pattern: Further, we integrate / and decide in which level.
boundary: the scale must have been named.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name the scale unless it is the one used.

units.function: state an optimization as choosing a vector so a sum lands on a surface

original_instantiations: By picking a direction of improvement so that the current state plus that step lands on the target, the upgrade becomes a picture.
Choose the step whose sum with the present position meets the surface, and the optimization is visible.

units.source_excerpt: By choosing an optimization vector such that the vector sum of these two vectors reaches the surface, the process of optimization is visualized.
units.reusable_pattern: By choosing [the decision object] such that [the condition], [the process] is visualized.
reusable_elements: occurrences: summary, third paragraph.

pattern: By choosing X such that / the process is visualized.
boundary: a figure must actually show it.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim visualization without the figure.

units.function: close the method list with the extension and its purpose

original_instantiations: Finally, we build a method for reading how the size of a firm changes the weight of each part, so the same model travels to other firms.
Last, we add a way to let the scale of a company shift the importance of the parts, so the assessment carries over.

units.source_excerpt: Finally, we set up the Scale-Demand method so as to analyse the influence of the scale on the importance of the three components.

boundary: the method must be the last one built.
prohibited_generalizations: Do not copy the method name.

units.function: grant a use, then escalate the difficulty past it

original_instantiations: Data do support decisions. But with so much of it produced, many firms struggle even to keep it, let alone to turn it into an advantage.
The records are genuinely useful. Still, the volume makes them hard to preserve, and harder still to exploit.

units.function: draw the necessity of the system from the difficulty just stated

original_instantiations: Consequently, a properly run system is urgently needed by any firm that wants to get value out of its records.

units.source_excerpt: Consequently, a well-operated data and analytics system is urgently needed for every corporation which desires to derive value from data assets.

units.function: decompose the system into the parts the model will use

Broadly, the system splits into three components, and the model treats each one.

units.source_excerpt: Generally speaking, a D&A system consists of three components, people, technology and process.

prohibited_generalizations: Do not add components the model never uses.

units.function: announce that the work is organized as numbered steps

With the setting established, we take the tasks in order.

units.function: hand the whole plan to a flow chart

original_instantiations: To keep the order of the work clear, the whole process is drawn in the figure.
So the sequence of what we do can be seen at a glance, we put it in a flow chart.

units.source_excerpt: For better arranging our process of problem solving, the flow diagram of our work is shown in Figure 1.

units.function: promise that every assumption carries its justification

original_instantiations: To make the problems tractable we adopt the following assumptions, and each one is justified.
We simplify with a short list of assumptions, every one of them backed by a reason.

original_instantiations: Assumption: the records we use are accurate. Justification: they come from official sources, so we take them as correct.
We assume the experts are equally qualified. The reason is that the weighting method gives us no way to tell them apart.

units.function: justify dropping indicators by invoking a named principle

original_instantiations: By the Pareto principle, most of an outcome comes from a small share of its causes, so we keep only the key indicators.
Since a few causes drive most of the result, we concentrate on those and leave the minor ones out.

units.source_excerpt: According to the Pareto principle, roughly 80 percent of consequences come from 20 percent of causes. To assess the maturity level, we concentrate on key parts of the cause.

Everything we abbreviate is set out below.

original_instantiations: It is widely accepted that a good indicator is specific, measurable, attainable, relevant and time-bound. We care most about measurability, without ignoring the rest.

units.source_excerpt: The entropy weight method is an objective weighting method, based on the principle that the greater the degree of dispersion, the greater the degree of differentiation, and thus the more information can be derived.
